wall_clock_verification.method: Standalone Node script (outside vitest, process.on('unhandledRejection') instrumented) racing a fn() that rejects 200ms AFTER a 50ms budget already won — zero unhandled rejections observed, callWithBudget correctly returned BUDGET_EXHAUSTED. Separately, a reviewer-authored vitest harness (temporarily added to src/__tests__/, deleted immediately after running, never committed) called reconcileInstanceEngineDrive directly with a port whose 3 methods all return `new Promise(() => {})` (permanently pending, never resolves, never rejects) and driveDeadlineMs=80 — measured wall-clock elapsed=82ms, res.ok=false, res.code=ENGINE_DRIVE_TIMEOUT, res.stage='poll'. This is ~500x faster than the ~40s+ withRetry worst case the spec's F-2 finding was about, confirming the deadline mechanism actually bounds a genuinely-hung engine call, not just a slow-but-eventually-settling one.

db_lane.result: ran live against a throwaway Postgres 16 (port 55433, isolated from sibling worktrees' own DB containers already occupying 54432/55432) — applied all 105 migrations, built fitness:db test template, ran ci/checks/db/engine-drive-generic.db.test.ts: 3/3 pass.
